mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY > 3% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which is typically associated with a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases > 0.5% in 1 month and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS declines for 3 consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% YoY signals a strong supply-side expansion, which typically boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO YoY > 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening monetary policy, which typically reduces borrowing costs and boosts corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and falling nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to a broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls simultaneously and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) combined with a decrease in real final sales (RSAFS) signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST and RSAFS both decline and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% signals higher borrowing costs, which typically reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases > 0.5% during a tightening cycle and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances, the hypothesis fails.
